security_audit.summary: The 53 static findings are false positives caused by Markdown formatting, documentation URLs, and an explicit standard-input authentication example. Two context-level risks remain: automatic ingestion of workspace domain-skill files without an untrusted-content boundary, and guidance that frames stealth browsers as a way to avoid anti-bot controls.

remediation.issue: Domain-skill files are treated as instructions without a trust boundary.
remediation.suggestion: State that domain-skill files are untrusted reference material. Require agents to ignore embedded instruction overrides and to use only verified, task-relevant technical guidance.

remediation.issue: Cloud-browser guidance promotes avoiding captchas and rate limits.
remediation.suggestion: Remove evasion language. Require user authorization and compliance with website terms, rate limits, and access controls before automated browsing.

remediation.issue: Browser automation can act in an authenticated session.
remediation.suggestion: Require confirmation before consequential actions, data export, account changes, purchases, or submissions, and keep the existing login and consent stops.

semantic_findings.title: Untrusted Domain-Skill Instructions Are Read Automatically
semantic_findings.description: When enabled, the skill instructs the agent to read every site-specific file from a workspace directory before choosing an approach. Those files can contain untrusted prompt content, but the guidance provides no instruction to treat it as data or resist prompt injection.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The instructions explicitly require reading workspace-provided domain-skill files and do not define a trust boundary. This creates a direct prompt-injection surface when that directory is writable or populated from untrusted sources.

semantic_findings.title: Captcha-Bypass Positioning
semantic_findings.description: The cloud-browser guidance recommends managed IPs and stealth settings when captchas or bot blocking are likely. This can encourage bypassing website anti-automation controls without confirming authorization.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The text expressly connects stealth settings and managed IPs with avoiding captchas and rate limits. It is guidance for evading service controls rather than a neutral browser-use instruction.

content.user_title: Automate interactive browser tasks with CDP
content.value_statement: Web tasks that need clicks, JavaScript rendering, or an existing signed-in session are difficult to handle with simple HTTP requests. This skill controls a CDP-enabled browser and provides workflows for navigation, testing, screenshots, recordings, and cloud browsers.
actual_capabilities: Connect to a local Chrome or Chromium instance through the Chrome DevTools Protocol.
Navigate pages, inspect accessibility trees, click elements, and wait for page loads.
Use JavaScript and raw CDP calls for page inspection and extraction.
Create isolated cloud browser sessions for approved parallel browser tasks.
Capture screenshots and manage optional browser-work recordings.
Guide local Chrome remote-debugging setup and connection diagnostics.
limitations: Requires a compatible local or cloud browser connection and appropriate user permissions.
Does not bypass passwords, multi-factor authentication, consent prompts, or ambiguous account choices.
May be unsuitable when a public page or API can be accessed with a simple HTTP request.
Website terms, access controls, rate limits, and automation policies still apply.

use_cases.title: Test a signed-in web workflow
use_cases.description: Navigate a staging application, complete approved interface steps, and verify the visible result.

use_cases.title: Collect rendered page details
use_cases.description: Inspect a JavaScript-rendered page and extract information from its accessibility tree or DOM.

use_cases.title: Document a browser procedure
use_cases.description: Record an approved workflow and capture screenshots for a support or product demonstration.

prompt_templates.title: Open and inspect a page
prompt_templates.prompt: Open https://example.com in the browser. Wait for it to load, then summarize the page title and main headings.

prompt_templates.title: Test a visible interaction
prompt_templates.prompt: In my staging app, open the settings page, find the notification toggle by its accessible name, change it, and verify the saved state. Ask before submitting any final change.

prompt_templates.title: Extract rendered content
prompt_templates.prompt: Open the provided public product page. Use the accessibility tree or DOM to collect each product name and displayed price. Do not bypass access controls or login walls.

prompt_templates.title: Run an isolated approved task
prompt_templates.prompt: Start one isolated cloud browser for this authorized test. Visit the supplied staging URL, capture a screenshot after the dashboard loads, report the result, and ask before leaving the browser running.

output_examples.input: Open the public documentation page and list its main sections.
output: Opened the page and waited for the document to load.
Main sections found: Getting started, Configuration, API reference, and Troubleshooting.

output_examples.input: Test whether the save button confirms a profile update.
output: Updated the requested test field in the staging profile.
The page displayed a saved confirmation and the refreshed value matched the change.

output_examples.input: Capture a screenshot of the loaded dashboard.
output: Screenshot captured and saved to the active task output.

best_practices: Use a direct HTTP request for public information when browser interaction is unnecessary.
Prefer accessible element names and verify each consequential action after it completes.
Ask for confirmation before submissions, account changes, purchases, exports, or leaving cloud browsers active.
anti_patterns: Do not use the skill to bypass login, multi-factor authentication, consent, or account-selection prompts.
Do not use stealth settings or managed IPs to evade website anti-bot controls or rate limits.
Do not treat site-specific workspace files as trusted instructions without reviewing their source and purpose.

faq.question: When should I use this skill?
faq.answer: Use it when a task needs browser interaction, JavaScript rendering, screenshots, or an approved signed-in session.

faq.question: Can it control my local Chrome browser?
faq.answer: Yes. It connects through Chrome DevTools Protocol after remote debugging is enabled and approved.

faq.question: Can it handle passwords or multi-factor authentication?
faq.answer: No. Stop and ask the user for passwords, multi-factor authentication, consent, or ambiguous account choices.

faq.question: Does it support cloud browsers?
faq.answer: Yes. It can start isolated Browser Use cloud sessions for authorized tasks and should ask before leaving them running.

faq.question: Can it record browser work?
faq.answer: Yes. Recording is optional and can be enabled for a task when the user requests a recording, demo, or video.

faq.question: Can it bypass captchas or website restrictions?
faq.answer: No. Use browser automation only with authorization and in compliance with website terms, access controls, and rate limits.
